newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: White S.Africans get 50 years for pre-poll bombs.
newsitem.headline: White S.Africans get 50 years for pre-poll bombs.

text.p: Two white right-wing extremists who tried to bomb South Africa's historic 1994 elections into catastrophe have been jailed for 50 years each, local media reported on Saturday.

Cliff Barnard and Abraham Myburgh were sentenced in a Johannesburg court on Friday for their part in four bombings, part of a campaign to try to derail the April 1994 all-race polls that ended white minority rule and elected Nelson Mandela as the country's first black president.
A third co-accused, Jan de Wet, was jailed for 25 years for his part in one of the bombings the day before the elections which killed 10 people.
The three, all members of the neo-Nazi Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB), had been found guilty last year in absentia after they escaped from custody during their trial in March.
All three were caught in January this year, a month after four people died in a bombing claimed by a little-known right-wing group.
Barnard and Myburgh were convicted on 20 murder charges and 47 charges of attempted murder.
"No sentence can ever be an appropriate punishment for what they did to other people and to the community," the Citizen newspaper quoted the judge, Justice Flemming, as saying.
In sentencing, the judge also took into account submissions by the state that the accused had shown no sign of remorse.
A fourth man, Etienne le Roux, was sentenced last year to 29 years' imprisonment for the bombing campaign.
